Date: 2027-04-20 09:12 PDT
Subject: Renewal planning: multi-year + co-term across business units

Kim,

Thanks for the time this morning. High-level ask from our side: we want to convert next year's hosted usage into a 24-month commitment that covers three of our business units, with a staggered onramp that aligns to our product launch cadence. Primary constraints:
- Billing cadence needs to be quarterly (finance prefers Q billing).
- We want a single co-term for licensing across the three units but retain the ability for one unit to opt out at year 1 with a 90-day notice (opt-out clause).
- Can you include a true-up mechanism for actual usage vs committed monthly tokens and an annual reconciliation credit/charge?
- Concern around auto-renew: procurement will only accept if there is an explicit auto-renew opt-out window rather than perpetual auto-renew.

Also attaching our draft SOW and a short procurement checklist. Could you provide a skeleton mutual action plan and a draft term structure we can review?

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Cloud Platforms, Acme Cloud

Date: 2027-04-21 11:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: multi-year + co-term across business units

Ellen —

Appreciate the clear requirements and the SOW. High-level proposal to get us moving:

1) Structure: 24-month primary term with an optional 12-month early-exit on Unit C only (90-day notice) — preserves co-term for the other units.
2) Ramp schedule: 3-phase ramp over first 9 months (20% / 30% / 50% of committed monthly capacity) that maps to your launch windows; we can attach a phased usage band to the contract.
3) Billing: quarterly invoicing on calendar quarter with mid-quarter usage reporting for visibility. True-up: annual reconciliation with either credit or overage invoice (30-day net).
4) Auto-renew: we will include a 60-day opt-out window prior to renewal with a one-time written notice to avoid perpetual auto-renew traps.
5) Credits/Discounts: given the multi-year commit and co-term, we can offer a blended rate with a 7% starter credit in year 1 applied as an onboarding credit; any additional concession (e.g., extended SLA credits) we'd need approval from Marcus/Rev ops.

Next steps: I attached a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a proposed term summary. If that looks good, I can loop in contracts for a tailored amendment and generate a DocuSign for procurement. Also copying Marcus to confirm the concession bandwidth.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
